Can I ask you please to confirm the following: You've told us that with your brothers, you went to Hotel Pastrik and identified some clothing that you thought belongs to your father. And as a result of that identification, a set of remains were released to your family which you buried, believing to be your father; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOICA VLAHOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did you do your honest best to identify the clothes that you were shown?

utterances.speaker: MILOICA VLAHOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we did, but it was a long period involved between April and September. And the second thing, how could we know what they were wearing on that day? It wasn't that we saw them the following day, so it was difficult to establish.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: On this aspect of your testimony, there's no criticism at all. I entirely understand. But the fact is that you and your brothers, doing your honest best, all identified a set of clothing you thought was your father, which resulted in a body being released to you, which, later on it was discovered, following an exhumation and a DNA test, was the wrong person. It wasn't your father at all. That's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MILOICA VLAHOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Emmerson. I would seek one clarification but not from the witness but perhaps from the parties at this moment. But before we have a break, how much time would you need, Mr. Guy-Smith? How much time would you need, Mr. Harvey?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If I take any time at all - I'm going to have a conversation during the break - it would be no more than 10 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: That conversation will partly be with me, as a result of which I will decide whether -- but it will not be more than five minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then, Mr. Vlahovic, there may be - "may be" I say - a few more questions from other Defence counsel after the break. We'll have a break and we'll resume at -- for you, I'm telling you now, at -- we are not yet there, Madam Usher. We'll resume at approximately 20 minutes -- at 20 minutes past 4.00, but I have one further question for Mr. Emmerson before we adjourn. But the witness can leave already. Madam Usher, the witness can be escorted out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I ask for the following clarification: If there's any agreement between the parties on this event. Of course, if not, then we'll have to find out in a different way. Your questions implied that the witness had recognised the clothing of his father and that turned out to be not correct, at least a later DNA analysis showed that the body that was given to the family was not the body of his father.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What was not clear to me is was the clothing at that moment on the body when they recognised this or was it separate?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No. Separate. The way the identifications were done - and it's partly because the remains were in various states of decomposition - is that the clothing was removed from the remains and, I think, even cleaned and then spread out on tables, and families were invited to look at the clothing and conduct identifications in that way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And this is one -- and Your Honours will know I've been mentioning it in various documents at various stages in the pre-trial stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: There are -- of the positive clothing identifications that took place from the remains discovered at the canal, half of them turned out to be like this one, in error.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand that. But just for my understanding -- Mr. Dutertre, if you disagree, then, of course, I would like to hear from you. So if there are -- if we're talking about mistakes in the identification, but just correct me when I'm wrong, I still see two possibilities: That you identify the right clothing but they give you the wrong body, or that you make a mistake in identification of the body. We have no knowledge yet, so --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: In this particular instance, there is no body for the father, so the clothing that was identified was not taken from a body that could possibly be the father. In other words, all of the bodies that have been exhumed and DNA-identified, none of them are the father. The father's body has not been recovered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But at the same time, wasn't the body given to the family?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It was the wrong body. It was the body of someone else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I do understand. But -- okay. We'll perhaps have to learn more about this. Mr. Dutertre, if you want to add anything. I'm just trying to understand what the testimony is about.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, indeed, Your Honour. This issue will be raised in further details with video elements which will help you make your determination on this matter. What we know for sure is that, indeed, there may be some things taken from bodies which remain unidentified up to now, and it's difficult sometimes to establish correspondence between these and blood samples. There are still some unidentified bodies or cases. Now, body parts belonging to the mother of the witness were identified through DNA analysis, and I believe that there is an agreement on that particular point with the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If it helps, Your Honour, just to be absolutely clear, when the family went to the hotel, they could not find any clothing that corresponded to the mother, so no identification was made of the mother. They found clothing they believed to be the father's, and on the basis of that clothing and a comparison of ante and post mortem data, a set of remains was released to the family as being the father and nothing as being the mother. It then turned out subsequently that all of the remains that were exhumed for identification, including all of the unidentified remains that Mr. Dutertre refers to, were tested against the DNA of the family and it turned out that the body that had been released to the family as the father was in fact another man called Istref Krasniqi and one of the unidentified remains was the mother but none of the unidentified remains were the father.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you already for this clarification. It is for us to better be able to follow the evidence -- what the evidence is exactly about. I know there is some agreement. Therefore, I didn't want to ask the witness very specific questions if it's not an matter in dispute.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And a brief addition, Your Honour. I'll be brief, I promise. The human remains of the mother which were identified had to do with legs. They were bones from the legs and there was no clothing available, which explains the fact that there was no identification through clothing for the mother. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What, perhaps, may have confused me, that earlier mention -- it was mentioned "traditional recognition" and it now becomes clearer and clearer to me that this is not traditional recognition because usually in traditional recognition, you have both the body and the clothes often on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. By traditional identification, Your Honours should read "clothing identification coupled with a comparison of ante mortem and post mortem data," in other words, a person of a certain age with a gold tooth, or whatever it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Again, very briefly on that particular point. This is just an addition, again. I'm sure we'll talk about it later. But the circumstances in which all of these identification took place were a bit difficult, which explains the fact that the clothing had to be separated from the bodies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. There seems to be quite a lot of agreement. Of course, the Chamber would have preferred to have all this in written format so that we would have known about it already and not have to speculate and to guess what will come tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Sorry to say, but just a reminder, you will find a summary of this in the Defence pre-trial brief. It is set out there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but not as -- as an agreement?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, it reflects the agreed state of the evidence, and in the footnotes it should be reasonably identified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps I have not looked carefully enough. We will resume at 4.25.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Vlahovic, we were informed that there are no further questions by other counsel. Mr. Dutertre, before the Chamber considers whether we have any other questions, is there any wish to re-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, indeed, Your Honour, I would have a couple of questions to ask of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Vlahovic, I would like to ask you some further questions. First of all, as regard the tensions between the Albanian population and the Serb population in the area where you lived during the years preceding the conflict, Mr. Emmerson asked you if there had been specific problems with specific Albanian families. This is on page 70 of yesterday's transcript. Mr. Emmerson also asked you if there had been property disputes between certain Albanian families and Serb families. This is on page 71 of yesterday's transcript. When I questioned you on Tuesday, you said that Serbs had left the area, and you gave us a few figures about the number of students in the Ratis village, that is, Serb students, and for you this was an indication of the fact that the Serb population had left. In 1974 there were some 20 students; and in 1980, there were two students, Serb students, left when your brother completed school. My question is as follows: To your opinion, what is the weight to be granted to those property feuds or property disputes between Serb families and Albanian families in the decrease in the number of Serbs among the population of your village?

utterances.speaker: MILOICA VLAHOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think that was that important. There were property disputes. Perhaps the Serbs were trying to sell some land in the 1980s and 1990s and were unable to. But aside from that, there were no disputes at all. All this happened because of the attacks that were launched by the Albanians on the Serbs and all the intimidation that went on and all the damage caused to the Serbs, which is what I spoke about yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: I would like to move to another issue as regards the attendance in schools. Yesterday, Mr. Emmerson asked you lengthy questions on the school system in the 1990s. This is page 72 and 73 of yesterday's transcript. And in an answer that you gave to one of his questions, you indicated that in certain schools there were only Albanians, and you said that Roma were in the same schools as Serbs. Was that your idea of the situation in 1998? Were Roma in the same schools as Serbs? Does that also depict the situation prevailing in 1998?

utterances.speaker: MILOICA VLAHOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Roma went more to Albanian schools than to Serb schools, and the Siptars, of course, went to Siptar schools to be taught in their Siptar language. Something I forgot yesterday. It was sometimes the case that Serbs completed their schooling in Albanian in Decani, for example, or the elementary school where I taught in Glamoc area, there were two people called Lakicevic who were taught in Albanian, although they were ethnic Serbs. I was not aware of a single case where an Albanian or a Siptar completed their education in the Serbian language. Not a single case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Can you explain to us the difference between an Albanian and a Siptar in one sentence, how you were using this -- how you used these words?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Back in Kosovo, the Albanians were those living in Albanian, and the Siptars were those living in Kosovo, but that is the only distinction that's normally drawn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Mr. Vlahovic, as regards armed activities at the beginning of 1998, you said that on the 19th of April, 1998, your father had seen men shooting in the air close to your house - that's what you were told by your father - on the 20th. This reference can be found on page 57 of the transcript. Mr. Emmerson asked you if before the 20th of April you had already seen armed Albanian men on the roads or in the villages around your house in Donji Ratis. This is page 57 of yesterday's transcript. And you said no. Mr. Emmerson then asked you if the shooting that you could hear on a regular basis since the beginning of the month of April - I believe he was referring to the shooting coming from Glodjane - were the only signs of such activities and you said yes? I'd like to get a clarification on this particular point. When I questioned you on Tuesday, you referred to a certain number of incidents, the one involving Dragoslav and Mijat Stojanovic, brothers; the execution of Slobodan Prascevic, a retired policeman who was driving his car the beginning of March; the incident with the Culafic couple at the end of February, beginning of March 1998, whose house was attacked with a rocket-launcher; the attack with automatic rifles with shots coming from different directions against the three houses, Babovic at the end of February, beginning of March 1998; the shelling of the Orthodox church in Donji Ratis. This is on the transcript of the 20th of March, 2007. The question is as follows: How do you interpret this emergence before the 20th of April, 1998 of repeated violent acts against Serbs or against Serb property using often military weapons?

utterances.speaker: MILOICA VLAHOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You could put it that way, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I hesitate to rise because I can see how Mr. Dutertre gets to the position he has got to in the question that he's asked, but at the end of the day this witness has given evidence in respect of each of those incidents that he did not himself witness them and that, as far as I recall, there is no evidence as to who the perpetrators were. Now, on the basis of that background, apart from the Stojanovic incident, as to which we'll be hearing direct evidence that there was no evidence on even a hearsay basis as to who the perpetrators were. On the basis of that foundation, to ask a witness to express an opinion on who was responsible for those activities or why they had been carried out, in our submission, is not a proper question to be put to a witness of fact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Dutertre, I noticed that this is not the first question asking for an opinion at this moment. Of course, this witness is not an expert. But I -- of course, I do understand, Mr. Emmerson, that there's still not unclear about it. Nevertheless, if this witness has any -- if he would have any explanation which would be an explanation that could be given by a non-expert, then the Chamber would like to hear that. At the same time, Mr. Dutertre, could you please repeat your question and perhaps avoid words like, "how do you interpret this emergence" or -- you could ask perhaps the witness, whether he ever heard any explanation for the emergence, or -- because the witness is not an expert but -- so I do not disallow the issue to be raised and I'm not very strict on explanations and facts, but could you please try to keep the witness as close to the facts as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. It was not a trap. As a civil lawyer I was trying to find something which was not leading, but let me rephrase my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: How, Mr. Vlahovic, do you explain this series of repeated violent acts against Serbs, using military weapons?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me put the question to the witness. Mr. Vlahovic, are you aware of any facts that could serve to better understand the developments at that time in terms of violence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Probably these acts were committed in order to intimidate the local Serbs and in order to get them to move out of the area and in order to make Kosovo ethnically clean, so to speak. It may be clear that I'm only referring to my own native area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's not an answer to the question, as a matter of fact. Mr. Dutertre, these are the kind of risks we are running if we are asking for interpretations and explanations of certain developments. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: I'd like now to move to the way some Serbs were treated, some Serbs that you mentioned, treated by some Albanians that you also spoke about. Mr. Emmerson, yesterday, asked you about the treatment of the Markovic family and of Konstantin Stijovic. You said that the Markovic family had been escorted out of the region by Djevdet Sadikaj, and you also said that Djevdet Sadikaj had used a by-road because he was afraid to take the main road. This is on page 58 of yesterday's transcript. You also said that Konstantin Stijovic had told you he'd been released thanks to the intervention of Ramush Haradinaj's father, Hilmi Haradinaj. This is on page 81 of yesterday's transcript. Here's my question: Given the fact that you knew what was going on in the region, was the help given by the Markovic family and the release of Mr. Stijovic, was that something that occurred frequently?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: You mean the help to the Markovic family or the help by the Markovic family?

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The help received by the Markovic family and the release of Konstantin Stijovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I don't know. The Albanians helped often; neighbours helped. I never thought that at that time they would refuse to help.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Why is it that Djevdet Sadikaj, escorting the Markovic family, why was he -- why didn't he want to take the main road?

utterances.speaker: MILOICA VLAHOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most probably, or, rather, certainly there were armed people awaiting the Serbs on his way out. There's no other explanation. He could have taken the road through Rznic and Prilep or, alternatively, through Pozar and eventually reach Decani. Those were the two short-cuts. And he took the very long away around, at least twice that long, through the surrounding villages, and he eventually reached Pec municipality, meaning there were armed people there who were preventing Serbs from leaving the area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Dutertre, we need a factual basis for this last answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, absolutely, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: And I'd like to ask the witness whether this was an impression or whether this was something that he knew himself?

utterances.speaker: MILOICA VLAHOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I knew this personally. Even before this, there were rumours and there was what happened to Stojanovic. They had been known to stop people before and check people. They would release some of those people and hold some of them back.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, here the question again is vague, Mr. Dutertre, because the witness was asked why they took a certain road, and then the witness gave an explanation of the reasons. And then you asked him -- I asked for a factual basis for that, and then you asked him whether this was an impression or whether this was something that he knew himself. Now, we have two separate issues: Whether he knew about the circumstances which may have inspired the decision to take a certain road, and the second is whether this witness learned from whom that that was the reason. So let me try to get this clear from the witness. When you said this was your own knowledge, Mr. Vlahovic, did you refer to the circumstances which you thought would have caused this road to be taken, or were you referring to your knowledge that they took that road for that reason? Did anyone tell you or -- perhaps my question is not clear either. Did anyone tell you that that was the reason they took this road; and if not, what is, then, your source of knowledge that that was the reason they took this road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. Milojka told me at the time that they didn't have the courage to go through Ljumbarda or through Rznic because he probably could not save them, they perhaps would have killed them. And that's why he passed through Berane and reached Rausic -- Dasinovac, Vranovac [phoen], Berane and Rausic.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I don't like rising to interrupt, as Your Honours know. If Mr. Dutertre is going to explore this issue, then he, with respect, needs to explore it in the context of this witness's earlier testimony that Djevdet Sadikaj, the man who conducted this operation, was himself the KLA leader of Dashinoc.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Dutertre, if you have any -- until now we have only established what was the reason given, as we now learned by Milojka, why they took that road. If you want to further explore the matter, I think it would be fair to put it in the context of the testimony of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, but I think that this was in debate, you know, the role held by Djevdet Sadikaj. It was mentioned by Mr. Emmerson yesterday, if my memory serves me right. And furthermore, I had no other question apart from this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It wasn't mentioned by me. It was mentioned by this witness. I put it to him from his statement and he agreed with it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Dutertre has no further questions for the witness, so let's leave it at this for the time being.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: First of all, does the re-examination trigger any need for further questions? Then let's see whether, perhaps, a few questions from the Bench would trigger any further questions. Judge Hoepfel has one or more questions for you, Mr. Vlahovic. Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Yes, Witness, can we get back to this issue of your pistol. You were asked about that by Mr. Emmerson, and I would like to know, had you bought this or how else did you get it, and when, in which year?

utterances.speaker: MILOICA VLAHOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You submit a request to be authorised to keep a weapon and then this is authorised or not. Mine was authorised back in 1988, and I bought this weapon with my own money.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Thank you. And were you carrying this pistol, after you had last seen your parents, with you?

utterances.speaker: MILOICA VLAHOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sometimes I did and sometimes I didn't. Sometimes yes; sometimes no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: And at this occasion which was discussed in cross-examination, when you went -- where you saw your old car, were you there with your pistol? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: MILOICA VLAHOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I did not have a pistol on me, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: And the car, just this very special question, did this play any further role, then? Did you see it again after that time?

utterances.speaker: MILOICA VLAHOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I never went there again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have one question for you. Your testimony yesterday referred to the events of the 21st and 22nd of April. You said that you met a friend of yours. You went to Pec, from Djakovica to Pec. You gave the name of that friend, Duna Laka. You said: "I left with him for Pec to take a motor vehicle there on business." It was not clear to me what you meant by "to take a motorcycle there on business"? What kind of business in Pec? Your business? His business? Could you please explain.

utterances.speaker: MILOICA VLAHOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly. This friend and I, we got a 124 Mercedes in Djakovica, and we were about to take it to Pec.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: For what reason?

utterances.speaker: MILOICA VLAHOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because the owner was from Pec.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And what, then, was the business? That's unclear to me.

utterances.speaker: MILOICA VLAHOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To sign over the ownership of the car, which is done wherever the owner happens to be residing. One needs to have a contract drawn up and then, of course, rubber-stamped.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Do I then understand that you had sold that car?

utterances.speaker: MILOICA VLAHOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was the one buying it. I was making the purchase.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. That's clear to me. I have no further questions for you. Have the questions of the Bench triggered any need for further questions? Mr. Vlahovic, this concludes your testimony in this court. I'd like to thank you very much for coming to The Hague and for answering questions of both parties and of the Bench. Under normal circumstances, I would not instruct you not to speak with anyone about your testimony. That is not usual. Once you're excused, you can speak with anyone. However, in the present circumstances, and let me just ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just to be sure, Mr. Dutertre, no protective measures for coming witnesses, the immediate following witness? No. The next witness, as you may be aware of, is your brother. Although you can speak about your testimony, don't tempt your brother, who is not allowed if he has started his testimony, to speak with anyone. Don't engage in any conversations with him about your testimony with someone who is still testifying at that moment. So, therefore, it's a bit unusual, but I think it's better to refrain from further discussing the matter until you travel back. Then, Madam Usher, could you please escort the witness out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. Thank you for calling me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Dutertre, is it you or Mr. Di Fazio who is taking the next witness? Mr. Di Fazio. Madam Registrar, do we have any -- yes, we have marked for identification. Could you please read the documents? And I don't think that any of them are under seal, are they?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson -- one is under seal. Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm trying to recall which one it was that might be under seal, first of all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you give the number, then I'll have a look at it on my --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It's Prosecution Exhibit number 30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Dutertre, is there any need to have P30 under seal? From what I understand, it is a DNA report.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't believe so, Your Honour, but I'm wondering whether a decision had been made regarding the two photographs of the parents of the previous witness. They were marked for identification, but I'm not sure that they've been admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We're not going to try to find that out. You can communicate with the registrar to find out whether there's any failure yet. If so, then of course we'll repair that. Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, in all, there are eight documents that were referred to or used either before or during cross-examination. Documents 1 to 6, first of all, which I gave to Your Honours in written form yesterday have not, I think, formally been given an identification mark.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And so they will each need to be marked for identification, and I will tender them for consideration as exhibits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Of course if there are not any questions put to the witness in relation to them, because we had no translation, that's what you explained before. I suggest that, just as we did yesterday, that we invite Madam Registrar to make a list of those pending admission issues and pending issues for marking for identification, and that on the basis of that list we'll deal with it tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Is that acceptable to you as well, Mr. Di Fazio? MR. DI FAZIO: It is. It is suitable. And I was just going to say that we have a problem with them going into evidence at this moment because of translation; we're not satisfied with the accuracy of it, of the translations, in particular 5 and 6.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then, Mr. Emmerson, you're aware that there's still some work to be done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: These documents, which still need a description, will be marked for identification because they have been given to the Chamber, but at this moment we delay any further decision on admission into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just in order to deal with the matter in a procedurally and tidy manner, there are two other documents. One of them is the single sheet which was shown on the ELMO, which culls that material and was put to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And the final one is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I dare ask -- I asked you whether you wanted to tender it but you said "No," but you want to have it marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. I will be, in due course, inviting Your Honours to admit that as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At the same time, let's be very practical. We have a list of a couple of names. You read all these names to the witness and no other names apart from the names on that sheet --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- so there is a full record of what was on that sheet.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And if there was not, now it is. So we don't need to give a number to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. Well, the other document is the investigator's report of the interview with the Sadikaj family.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Which was Defence document identification 48 which needs to be marked for identification, and again will be tendered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, let's first deal with this report which is -- and that's an additional question, is not a full report because there are huge parts -- did you receive it in this shape?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. It's a redacted document disclosed to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: No objection to that, if Your Honours please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, I understand. But of course the Chamber is not always happy to have to deal with redacted documents because not only the Defence is losing some information about the context. The context could be totally irrelevant and it could be damaging if it would be disclosed. At the same time, the only party who has now been in a position to verify that is the Prosecution, and even the Chamber now -- and the Chamber doesn't usually like to be in the hands of the Prosecution completely on these matters, just as the Chamber would not like to be in the hands of the Defence completely in that respect. MR. DI FAZIO: I'm not quite sure where Your Honour is going. Do I understand Your Honours to be saying that you would -- you would like to see the full document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, that's at least one thing you could consider, but then of course we'd have to know from the Defence whether the Defence likes the idea that the Chamber sees the full document and the Defence does not.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think Your Honour can anticipate what the response to that would be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I'm good at guessing.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Apart from anything else, I wouldn't be in a position to make submissions as to on the significance of it. If it's to be looked at and be in any way part of the consideration, then obviously the Defence need to be in a position to make informed representations about it. I should indicate that most of the redactions in this document do not relate to this particular interview. There's a lot of other material before this interview which is where Your Honours see the very heavy black pages. But there is a section of about two or three lines redacted at the bottom of page 6, a similar section at the top of page 7, and another larger section afterwards. In other words, within the interview, there are two short sections of redaction and it's possible that the third one is also relating to this or it could be relating to something else altogether. But as far as the very large redacted areas on pages 1, 2, 3, 4, and 5 are concerned, it's plain, I think, that those relate to inquiries other than inquiries with this particular witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. So there you accept that. Would it be a good idea that perhaps Mr. Di Fazio tries to convince you that the other portions -- because we do not know whether it's relevance, whether it's confidentiality, what the reasons are. If you could try to resolve that. Sometimes even a solution is that you just show the original unredacted copy and say, Do you see that this is not related, or there are sometimes ways of finding a solution where both parties would agree. And if both parties agree, then, of course, the Chamber would have less reluctance to accept it in this format.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: We will discuss it between ourselves. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. But a number -- it needs a number anyhow, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, actually, both the documents have already been given the numbers. It's D14 and D15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. Then we'll wait to see whether there are any -- at the same time, I'm a bit hesitant, Mr. Emmerson, because what happens is that you're provided with the redacted document, you do not complain about receiving a redacted document, you are the one who tenders into evidence the document, and now the Chamber is starting making trouble. That's a bit the world upside down. Nevertheless, I think for the Chamber to accept redacted documents, if the Defence is happy with it and stays happy with it, then we'll be happy with it as well, I take it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: May I discuss it with Mr. Dutertre and then resolve it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then we'll hear from you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Then the six documents, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, Madam Registrar, that were provided to the Chamber and served as an introduction to the cross-examination of the last witness, could you please give numbers for these documents.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, number 1 will be Exhibit number D16, marked for identification; number 2 will be Exhibit number D17, marked for identification; number 3, Exhibit number D18, marked for identification; 4, D19, marked for identification; 5, D20, marked for identification; and number 6 will be Exhibit number D21, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. None of them under seal, Mr. Emmerson, I take it? No. Then any further issue in relation to documents? If not, Madam Usher, would you please escort the next witness into the courtroom. And that would be, Mr. Di Fazio? MR. DI FAZIO: I'm sorry, I hadn't realised that was a question. It's the brother, Goran Vlahovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I'm anxious not to make any mistake, because we find a lot of family names. MR. DI FAZIO: At least that's who I think is walking through the door. I'm pretty sure it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Vlahovic. At least I take it that you're Mr. Vlahovic. Before you give evidence in this court, you are required to make a solemn declaration that you'll speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. The text is now handed out to you by Madam Usher. I'd like to invite you to make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Vlahovic. Please be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You'll first be examined by Mr. Di Fazio, who's counsel for the Prosecution. Mr. Di Fazio, you may proceed. Examination by Mr. Di Fazio:

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Mr. Vlahovic, as you've just heard, my name is Di Fazio and we haven't spoken before. I just want you to understand that I'm one of the Prosecutors in this case. MR. DI FAZIO: Madam Usher, I wonder if you could move the ELMO. I can't see the witness's face. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Now, can you tell us the name of the village in which you were born --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, especially in this family situation, should we not start with the full name and date of birth so that we have -- MR. DI FAZIO: Certainly. I can get those details. Not a problem. And I'm grateful to Your Honour for reminding me.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Can you give us your date of birth?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: 16th of June, 1974.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: And just for the record, your full name, please?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: Goran Vlahovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber where you were born?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: In Decani.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Is that Decani municipality?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: And a few more specifics. What village in that municipality, please?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: Ratis.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: It's not in dispute in this case that there are two Ratises: Gornji and Donji. Which one?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: Gornji. Gornji Ratis.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: And if I ask -- if I asked your ethnicity, what is your answer?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: I'm a Serb.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Thank you. I want you to cast your mind back to early 1998. At that period of time did you have a job, an occupation; and if so, what was it?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I worked as a conductor in Decani.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Conductor of what?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: The company called Autoprevoz on the line between Decani and Pec.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: And just so there's no doubt about that, that's a bus company. You're a bus conductor; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: And how long had you been working at that job in early 1998?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: Since 1996.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: What sort of work did you do before that?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: I worked in a sawmill in Decani.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Did you do military service in your youth?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Where?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: In Pristina.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: And how long for?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: Twelve months.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: And did you specialise in any particular aspect of military training during that year?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Did you ever train as a policeman?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: In 1997 or early 1998, were you in any reserve force? And by "reserve force," I'm talking about any sort of reserve police force or reserve army force.

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Okay. I would also like some more personal details, if you don't mind. Could you -- I'd like you -- to take you through your family, starting with your parents, give us the names of your parents, and then start with your siblings and start at the top with the oldest one, and tell us the name of all your siblings, brothers and sisters, in descending order. So let's start with your mother and father and then tell us the rest of them.

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: Milovan Vlahovic, Milka Vlahovic --

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: They're your parents?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Okay. And now your siblings, starting with the eldest down to the youngest?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: Nada Vlahovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: You can keep going.

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: Novak Vlahovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Just keep going and keep going until you've got to the end of the family.

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: Miloica Vlahovic, Rade Vlahovic, Natalia Vlahovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Thank you. In early 1998, where did your parents reside?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: In the village of Gornji Ratis.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: And just so you understand, I'm asking you -- when I say the early period of 1998, I'm talking about the period January, February, March of 1998. Now, in about that period of time, where did you live?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: I was also living in Ratis.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Now, is that in exactly the same village, namely, Gornji Ratis, or is it Donji?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: The same village, Gornji Ratis.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: And in that village did you live at the same house, in the same house, the same building, as your parents, or did you have your own separate house?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: In the same house.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: How did you get to your work in that period of time?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: We travelled by car.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Can I just ask you to slow down with your answers. Just wait a little moment because your answers have to be interpreted, and it makes it easier for me and for everyone here if you just slow it down a bit. So just listen to my question carefully and then answer it, okay? You say: "We travelled by car." Who travelled by car from Gornji Ratis to work?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: My brother and I.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Which brother are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: Novak.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: And what sort of car was that?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: A Mercedes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: And do you have a model on that, please? What type of Mercedes are you speaking about?

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Did all of your siblings have their own cars, or was that the only one in the family?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: We had other cars as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Mercedes, other Mercedes, or was that the only one in the family?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: There was another Mercedes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: And what model was that?

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: In early 1998 - and remember that I'm again talking about that period of time January, February, March - did you have any problems in making the commute from Gornji Ratis to your work-place?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: We didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Were you aware or did you have any information that any of your siblings had any trouble?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: Not that I know of.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Thank you. And I'd just like to know some details about the people who lived in Gornji Ratis. Were there Serb families living there?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. There were four households.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Thank you. And what about the remainder of the village? What ethnicity were they?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: Albanians and Catholics.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Okay. And when you say "Catholics," do you mean Albanian Catholics or some other ethnic group who were Catholic?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: Albanians.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: And just finally on this issue. You say there were four Serb households living in the village. In terms of households, how many households of Albanian ethnicity would you say there were in that village?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm not asking you to provide absolute precision, but can you give us an answer? I'd just like to know if four households were in the majority or in the minority? Can you give us even an approximate idea?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: A minority.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Minority Serb; is that what you mean?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Thank you. I've asked you some questions about the first few months of 1998, and I asked you some questions about whether you or your family members had any problems in commuting, travelling in the area, and you said no.

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: We didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Just remember what I said about waiting. Let me finish my questions. I'm a bit of a slow-speaker so just wait on, okay? Was it the same in April? Did you have trouble-free commuting from Gornji Ratis to the bigger towns in the area?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, by the 20th of April, approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: I'm going to come to that date in a moment. But up until that time, you had no complaints or you couldn't -- you didn't have any trouble in getting from your village to any of the larger towns, Pec or Decani, and so on?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: No, there were no problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Very well. I want you to turn your attention now to the period of time around the 20th of April. First of all, around the 20th of April, were you still residing in Gornji Ratis with your parents?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did, until the 21st.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: And on the 21st, did you go to work or did you remain in Gornji Ratis? Can you tell the Trial Chamber what you did on that day?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: I went to work.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: How did you get to work on that day?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: By car.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Which car?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: The Mercedes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: And did you go to work alone on that day, or were any of your family, or indeed anyone else for that matter, was anyone else with you?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: With my brother.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Which one? Give us a name, please.

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: Novak.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: What was Novak's job at that time?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: He was employed with Autoprevoz Pec.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Sorry, was that the same company that you worked for?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: What was -- thank you. And what was Novak's job with Autoprevoz?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: He was a driver.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Did your parents have a telephone at their house?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Thank you. On that day that you left for work, on the 21st of April, 1998, did you see your parents?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: We saw them on that day and never again.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Did you go to work on that day and carry out your normal duties?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Did you try and get back to your house or your home that day?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: You say: "Yes, we did." When you say "we did," who are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: My brother and me.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: And is that Novak?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Well, did you have any success?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: No, none.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber why not? What prevented you from getting back home?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: They didn't let us. The roads were blocked.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: All right. Now, let's take this step by step. How did you find out that the roads were blocked? And what even caused you to make any inquiry or -- let me rephrase that. How did you find out that the roads were blocked?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: The police wouldn't allow us through. They wouldn't allow us to go there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Which police, located where precisely?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: At Decani.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: What I'd like you to do is try and give the Trial Chamber an idea of how it was that the police in Decani prevented you from going back. Was there a roadblock, a police roadblock? Did you receive information? Did you stop and speak to a policeman in the street? Did they come and see you? Please try and explain to the Trial Chamber how it was, how it came about, that the police informed you or led you to understand that you couldn't go back?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: The police were at Decani, and they didn't allow us through. They said the road was blocked and that one could not proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Were you and your brother in your car at that stage, intending to go home?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: So it was a roadblock. You were stopped by the police at a roadblock and they said, You can't go ahead. Do I understand your evidence correctly?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Did you make inquiries or ask the police why not?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. The road was blocked. One was no longer able to proceed and go there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Well, did you ask the police what sort of block it was? Was it a tree, a land-slide, armed men? What was it that blocked this road? The Trial Chamber would like to know.

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: They said there were armed men.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Did you try and get details from the police about what armed men?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: No. We asked no more questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Were you worried about your parents?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Well, being worried about your parents, did you try and make any other inquiries about whether it was possible to get back to them, back to Gornji Ratis and to your home and see if they were there?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: We tried but we couldn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, you tell the Trial Chamber what efforts you made. You say: "We tried ..." So tell them what you attempted to do?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: We tried to take the other road but it wasn't possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Just tell the Trial Chamber what the usual road was that you would take after you finish work and you're going back to Gornji Ratis. Which villages would -- just a minute, just a minute, just a minute. Let me finish. Which villages would you drive through to get back to Gornji Ratis on a normal day? And then after you've done that, try and tell -- tell the Trial Chamber which alternative route you sought after you heard that the normal route was blocked. So tell us about the normal route first and then the alternative that you tried.

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: First, Luka, Pozar, Ljumbarda, and Ratis. The other time, Crnobreg, Prilep, Rznic, Ratis.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: And how far did you get using the alternative route?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: As far as Prilep. No further.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: What stopped you there?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: The police.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Which police, please? The same kind of police which had stopped you before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, the same police.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: What police is that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Serb police.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: And did you get any information from the second police-block that told you you couldn't go ahead, about what the situation was up ahead?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: We were told the road was blocked, it wasn't possible to go there, and they didn't let us through.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: And on this occasion did you try and get any more details from the police, for example, what was blocking the road, when it might be unblocked, matters such as that?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: We tried but they were unable to tell us anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Either at the first block or the second block that you've told us about- I'm talking about the roadblocks by the police- did you get any -- find out from the police what or who was blocking the road?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: They just told us there were armed men but that was all they told us.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: All right. Faced with this situation, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: We returned to Decani.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: And in the following days, did you make attempts to get back to Gornji Ratis?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: We tried but it was no longer possible. They didn't let people through.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Now, you say: "We tried ..." Again, I'd like you to tell the Trial Chamber how you made these efforts. You told us that you and Novak had tried to drive back. Who tried to make the efforts to get back to Gornji Ratis?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: Novak and I.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: And was that in the same way, getting into your car and trying to find a road that would take you there?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. We got into our car and we took that one road. There was no other way to go.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Sorry to interrupt. Who was driving?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Novak was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: And did you have any success in the following days using this method of getting into your car and trying to drive up there?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: No, none.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Why couldn't you get through?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: The road was closed. They didn't let us through.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: And do I understand what you're saying is that the police had roadblocks and they wouldn't let you through? Is that -- do I understand that correctly, or someone else wouldn't let you through?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: The police didn't let us through.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Were you in touch with any other members of your family apart from Novak in those first few days after you -- after the 21st of April?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Who were you in touch with?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: With Rade, with Mico.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Did your brothers make any attempts to establish contact with your parents; and if so, what attempts?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: They tried the same as we had but they were not successful.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: What do you mean by that? They tried to drive up in cars as well but were turned back? Do I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Okay. Apart from the method of getting into a car and trying to drive up there, was any other method adopted to try and make contact with your parents?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: We didn't keep trying. It just wasn't possible. We tried to go by car but that was it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: You've mentioned -- MR. DI FAZIO: Sorry, if Your Honours would just bear with me for a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Did Rade, your brother Rade, have any Catholic Albanian friends in early 1998?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he did, over in Djakovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Did you -- are you aware of him enlisting the aid of any such person to try and make contact with your parents?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: What do you know about that? Can you tell the Trial Chamber what your brother did?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: He tried to send someone over to check if they were still in their house.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Okay. Do you know the name of this person whom he tried to send over to check on the house?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: Nuo Alakaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Did you speak to Nuo Alakaj yourself or was it only Rade who had contact with Nuo?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: Just Rade.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Were you ever present when Rade spoke with Nuo Alakaj about going to see your parents?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Did Rade ever tell you of any results of this attempt?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: What did he say to you?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: He said when Nuo had gone there, they were no longer around. They had taken them away by that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Do you -- thinking back to the 21st of April, about how long after that would you say that you found out that Rade had enlisted the aid of Nuo Alakaj? About how long?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Did this method of using an agent or someone, a friend, to go and try and find out about what had happened to your family, did any other attempts occur using the same method, perhaps with different people, that you're aware of?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. My cousin went over to see a neighbour, Faza Haradinaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Who is your cousin?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: Mica.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: And what's Mica's surname?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: Vlahovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: And did -- MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours would just bear with me. What time would Your Honours want to take the break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Within the next five minutes. If this would be a suitable moment. MR. DI FAZIO: It would.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We'll take a break, Mr. Vlahovic. Yes, Mr. Emmerson, does the witness need to stay for this?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Not necessarily.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Usher, could you please escort the witness out of the courtroom? We'll have a break for 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It simply relates to the arrangements over the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Purely for the witness's comfort, I wonder if he might be accompanied during the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The witness to be accompanied?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Exactly so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh, that's ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: First of all, you do not give any reasons, and apart from that, Mr. Emmerson, the practice is that the witnesses will spend the break in the presence of someone working in the Victims --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: In that case, I needn't -- that's exactly --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: They're not free to leave the building or to leave --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: That's all I was seeking to clarify, Your Honours, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we'll resume at five minutes past 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, please proceed. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: You mentioned your cousin who you -- assisted you in making some inquiries, and I think you said his name was -- just give us his name again, please?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: Miloica Vlahovic, the brother.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: What's the short -- what's the diminutive, the short version, of Miloica Vlahovic? Miloica in particular?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters didn't catch the answer. MR. DI FAZIO: I'll repeat my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Did anyone have a short version of his name? His friends, did they call him Miloica or did they use a shortened nickname?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: Mica.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: And where did this gentleman live?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: In Ratis.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: And what was his job?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: He was a teacher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Excuse me. You said Miloica Vlahovic, the brother, and you were asked about a cousin. Is he a brother or a cousin? Could you clarify, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Brother. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Earlier, just before the break, you were talking about an attempt to enlist the aid of a gentleman named Faza, and you mentioned that a cousin approached this man. What was the name of the cousin?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: My brother sent Faza over. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours just give me a moment, I just want to check the transcript, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Whilst that's done, I think Mr. Di Fazio may have a gender problem. I don't think Faza is a woman -- I'm sorry, I don't think Faza is a man; I think Faza is a woman. MR. DI FAZIO: I'm actually grateful for that, thank you. Yes. Thank you to Defence counsel for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Just before your -- the break, you said: "My cousin went over to see a neighbour, Faza Haradinaj." I asked you: "Who was your cousin?" You said: "Mica." And I asked: "What's Mica's surname?" And you said: "Vlahovic." Now, do you have a cousin named Mica Vlahovic, or Mica Vlahovic?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: No. That's my brother Mica, Miloica Vlahovic. That's the brother.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: That's clear. Thank you. And did your brother go and make inquiries of this person, this lady, Faza Haradinaj?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. She lived in Djakovica but in the same village, and my brother went there to speak to her, and then she went there to have a look.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: All right, thank you. That's clear enough. And were you there when your brother spoke to Faza and asked her to carry out this task, or is it something that your brother told you about?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: No, my brother told me.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Did you ever hear any -- if there were any results, whether Faza made contact or whether she was able to get any news about your parents?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. She told my brother that she'd been there. She had been to the house and they were in the house at that time, but they weren't allowed to leave their home or, indeed, to move about.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Now -- and your brother told you this and that's Rade, I believe; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: No, Mica.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm grateful to you for that correction. Just thinking back now, I know it's a long time, but have you got any idea of just precisely how Mica reported this to you, in particular what he said to you about them -- about them being in the house and not being able to leave? What sort of words did he use, if you can remember? If you can't, say so.

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Thank you for that. Are you aware of any other attempts to establish contact with your parents through this method of using people to go and speak to them?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: All the people who your family enlisted to try and make contact with your parents in their village, what ethnicity were they?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: Albanians and Catholics.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Meaning also Albanians; no? MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Can you answer His Honour's question?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Thank you. Please go on. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Anyway, the result is that all of these efforts were fruitless, and you never saw your parents alive again; correct?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: No, we never saw them again.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: How old were your parents then?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: My mother was about 58, and my father 53, or thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I want to ask you some questions about your brothers and their jobs. Novak, you've told us, was a bus driver, I believe. How long had he been doing that job as at early 1998?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Can you tell us this: Had he had that job all his life or was he new to the job? He was a new bus -- a bus driver?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: No. He started working as a driver back in 1991, I suppose.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Had he ever worked as a policeman or a soldier, professional soldier?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: What job did your brother Rade have?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: Rade was with the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: And how long had he been a policeman?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: Since 1990 or possibly 1991. I can't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Was he doing that job in early 1998, and in particular in April of 1998?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Where was he stationed? Where was his day-to-day office or reporting place?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: Djakovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Do you know what sort of policeman he was? Perhaps I should be a little clearer about that. Policeman do all sorts of different jobs. Some are investigators, some are detectives, some are clerks in offices. What sort of job did your brother Rade do in the police?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: Just a regular police officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Uniformed?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Did he continue doing that work throughout the rest of the year after your parents disappeared, or after they were last seen alive by your family?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: And the brother Miloica, what was his job?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: He was a teacher.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Do you know a gentleman named Zvonko Markovic?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: What was his job in early 1998?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: He worked with the post office. He was a postman.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: That's right. And where was he working in April -- I didn't get that. Could you just repeat that, please?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: In Streoce.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Did he ever work in Rznic?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Did he ever become a policeman or was he ever in the reserve police?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: Not that I know of.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Did you have any contact with him in 19 -- let me rephrase that. After your parents were last seen alive by you and your family, did you have any contact with Zvonko Markovic by any chance?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: We saw each other sometimes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Where? Where did you see each other?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: In Decani.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Do you know a gentleman named Halil Sadikaj?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Do you know a gentleman named Salih Sadikaj?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Do you know the village of Dasinovac?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: About how far away is Dasinovac from your village?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: Five or 6 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Do you know of a village in your area called Dashinoc, or Dashinoc?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Does Dasinovac have any other name or is it known by any other name?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I think there may be some misunderstanding here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps about exactly how the name was pronounced.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: We know, it's a matter of geographical fact, that Dashinoc is the Albanian name for Dasinovac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We find that, of course, in the indictment and you are using the two sometimes Dasinovac, although you usually refer to the Albanian version of this village. Let's put it directly to the witness. Witness, the Chamber, until now has heard some evidence and has seen maps in which it appears that Dasinovac, in Albanians, is called Dashinoc. Is that something that sounds familiar to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Dasinovac, yes, that does. Dashinoc, no, that one doesn't.
