utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Many villages in your area have names both in, could I say, Serbo-Croat and in Albanian. Have you ever heard of an Albanian name of the village of Dasinovac, so the Albanian equivalent of Dasinovac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I suggest that any further examination, although the distance, 5, 6, kilometres, but perhaps not as the crow flies, but let's not make matters more complex. Counsel are invited to refer to Dasinovac if they would have had the choice. Please proceed. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: In September of 1998, did you go to the village of Dasinovac?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: In April of 1988 [sic] did you go there?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: What about any other month between April and September? Did you go to that village?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: No, we didn't. One couldn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Then, Mr. Emmerson, you are the first one to cross-examine the witness. Mr. Vlahovic, you'll now be cross-examined by Mr. Emmerson. He's the counsel for Mr. Haradinaj. Mr. Emmerson, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Vlahovic, you told us just a few moments ago when you first started giving evidence that you yourself have never served in any reserve police force in 1997 or 1998; is that right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did you ever serve in any reserve police force at any time? Pardon? I didn't catch your answer.

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And your brother Novak, did he ever serve in any reserve police force at any time?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but I don't know when.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So he did, but you don't know when it was?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Was it during the war?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Forgive me, but I thought you were just asked a question about that by Mr. Di Fazio. We'll have to check the transcript for just a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm looking at page 88, line 12 -- lines 12 and 13.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: "Have you ever worked as a policeman ..." You were asked by Mr. Di Fazio about Novak: "Had he ever worked as a policeman or a soldier, a professional soldier?" And you said: "No." Did Novak work as a policeman or didn't he?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: He was in the reserve force.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And people in the reserve force, Mr. Vlahovic, they wore uniforms, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And they carried AK-47 automatic rifles, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know what you mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: They carried automatic weapons, didn't they? You know what an automatic weapon is, don't you, Mr. Vlahovic?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they did, but I don't know what kind of weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did you see your brother Novak with automatic weapons at any time, or an automatic weapon at any time?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: He had some weapons, but I don't know what kind.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And Zvonko Markovic, what about him? You told us a moment ago, as far as you knew, he was not in any reserve police force. That's not true, is it, Mr. Vlahovic?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know that he was. He used to work in Streoce as a postman.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: He was your cousin, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Your families were quite close, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You saw each other often, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: Not often.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Vlahovic, correct me if I'm wrong, he has a brother, doesn't he, Zvonko? Sorry, I didn't catch your answer. He has a brother, doesn't he?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he does.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: What's his name?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: Rade.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And as far as you know, was Rade in the police of any kind?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Right. So let's just be clear about the situation. As far as you're concerned, you did know that Novak was a reserve police officer; correct?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: I knew.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But you did not know that Zvonko and Rade Markovic, your cousins, were both reserve police officers?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Does it come as a surprise to you to learn that they both made witness statements in which they acknowledge that they were reserve police officers during this period of time? Does that come as a surprise to you?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know about that. I wasn't here.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So it never came up in conversation in your family, that those two cousins of yours were members of the reserve police?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: Not in our family.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Vlahovic, I'm just going to tell you what your brother has just told us on oath about you. He says in his evidence: "I believe that he," Goran, "was in the reserve police, too." He was asked: "Did you see him in uniform and with a weapon?" And he said: "Most probably I did." And then he was asked: "So do I have it right that of the four brothers, you, Miloica, are the only one who wasn't in the police?" And he said: "Yes." Now, Mr. Vlahovic, were you in the police?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can you imagine any reason why your brother would think you were?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. He may have been mistaken.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: How often were you seeing Miloica at this time?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: I was in Montenegro and I saw him occasionally.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Sorry, when were you in Montenegro?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: In 1998 and in 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: When did you leave in 1998, and when did you return to Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: I left, I think, in June 1998. I don't know the exact date.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And when did you come back?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: When we found our father in September, and then I left again.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And is it your evidence that you were never in Kosovo between June 1998 and September 1998?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: No, I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And after September, 1998, were you in Kosovo then?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And were you in the police then, the reserve police?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And your brother Rade, you said he was a regular police officer. What do you mean by "a regular police officer"? What is the distinction between a regular police officer and some other kind of police officer?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: He was working all the time. He was in active duty.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Do you know what any kind of -- do you know of any kind of special force in the police in that area at that time?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You're not aware of the police having any kind of paramilitary force?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Have you heard of the PJP, Mr. Vlahovic?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So your brother Rade, I suggest, was a paramilitary police officer in the specialist unit called the PJP. Is that something you didn't know?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: See, Mr. Vlahovic, I suggest that you were not only in Kosovo but in Dashinoc at the beginning of September 1998, and that you were seen there with your brothers taking part in the looting of Albanian houses and the beating of an elderly gentleman called Shaban Sadikaj.

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: That's not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And further, that in April 1999, you were seen standing outside Decan Police Station when a convoy of Albanian refugees passed by and an elderly gentleman from Dashinoc called Ahmet Sokolaj, Ahmet Sokolaj, was pulled from the line, beaten and killed, and you were there, I suggest.

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: No, I wasn't there at all. It's not true.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, in one of your previous questions, you referred to Dashinoc and --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Dasinovac. Dasinovac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps you could ask the witness whether his answer would be the same --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- if you had located it in Dasinovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did you hear about the incident when an old man from Dashinoc was pulled from a convoy of refugees in Decan Police Station and beaten to death by Serb paramilitaries? Did you hear about that incident?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Stanisa Radosevic, is he a friend of yours?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did you know him at all?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: I knew him by sight.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I just ask you for a moment about the evidence you've given about Nuo Alakaj, the Albanian Catholic, who had a conversation, you say, with your brother Rade. I just want to be clear what your evidence is on this. You told us, I think, before the break, you were asked about Mr. Alakaj and you were asked: "Did you speak to him yourself or was it only Rade who had contact with Nuo?" And you said: "Just Rade." And you were asked: "Were you ever present when Rade spoke with Nuo Alakaj about going to speak with your parents?" And you said: "No." Is that right? Were you ever present when Rade spoke to Nuo Alakaj?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: No, I wasn't when -- I wasn't present when Rade spoke to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm just going to read to you a short passage from a statement that you made and signed in July 2004. So I'm going to read it slowly so that it can be translated to you, because these are words that you have put your name to. You said: "It was around July 1998 when I know that a Catholic Albanian friend of Rade went to the village with the intention of getting our parents out of the village but could not find them. I was with Rade when his friend came back from Gornji Ratis and told us that he had asked others in the village what had happened to our parents. The friend of Rade said that he had been told by others in the village that they had been taken away." Do you understand what I've just read to you?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, I'm not objecting, of course, at this point, but I wonder if Mr. Emmerson has read the last sentence of that paragraph. Oh, I certainly have. I certainly have.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The last sentence of that paragraph says: "I do not know the name of the Albanian friend of Rade." But in your proofing notes, that is to say, when you were interviewed on videolink, you explained the name of person you were referring to as Nuo Alakaj. We can check that if you like but I've got the reference for it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps we can ask the witness. When you had an interview with the investigators, as was just read to -- when you gave that statement, did you have anyone else on your mind when you're talking about the friend of Rade, anyone else than - let me find the name again --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Nuo Alakaj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- Nuo Alakaj. So when you gave that statement, did you -- when you didn't say at that time the name, were you referring to the person Nuo Alakaj?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then to whom were you referring? Were there two different persons that were sent to find out about your parents?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And the other one was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know the name.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Sorry, let's be clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, had you --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You told us before the break about Faza Haradinaj and Nuo Alakaj, and then Mr. Di Fazio asked you: "Were you aware of any other people sent to Gornji Ratis to look for your parents," and you said: "No." You told us in the clearest possible terms that the only people you were aware of were Faza Haradinaj, who was an elderly lady; is that correct? She's an elderly lady, isn't she, Mr. Vlahovic?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And a Catholic Albanian called Nuo Alakaj?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Are they, as you told us before the break, the only two people you were aware of who had been sent to speak to your parents?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: These are the ones that I know of. I don't know the name of this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So why was it that you told us before the break that you didn't know of any other attempts to send people to see your parents, Mr. Vlahovic?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: I was referring to the nameless one.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So this man you're now describing, this Catholic Albanian friend of Rade, this is a third person, is it?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. And that individual you were present for when he came back and spoke to your brother; is that right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Why didn't you tell us about that before the break, Mr. Vlahovic?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: I did mention the man.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, we've all got the transcript to consider. Let's go back to Nuo Alakaj, then. You say that Rade told you that Nuo Alakaj had gone to the village and your parents were no longer around; is that right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: That they had been taken away by that time; is that right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So Nuo Alakaj, who you hadn't heard speak, was saying exactly the same thing as this other Catholic Albanian who you now say you had heard speak; is that right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Which one came first in time?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: Nuo Alakaj was the first.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can you give us a physical description of Nuo Alakaj, please?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: It's been a long time. He was an elderly man.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And what about this other man that you're telling us about? What did he look like?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: He was also an elderly person.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You see, your brother Miloica has given evidence here today that Rade told him what Nuo Alakaj had said, and what Rade told Miloica was that Nuo Alakaj had told him, wrongly, that your parents had been released at Prilep and were free. Do you want to reconsider your evidence on any of these matters, Mr. Vlahovic?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: That's what I know. I don't know -- I don't know anything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You're sure, are you, about what you told us Rade told you?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So it would appear, wouldn't it, that Rade has said completely the opposite to your brother from what he said to you about the same conversation?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. That's what he told me.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Vlahovic, you and your brothers were heavily involved in retributive violence against the Albanian population of Dashinoc in September, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You were yourself a reserve police officer, as were all of your brothers except Miloica. You were in uniform and armed with automatic weapons, and you beat Albanians, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: GORAN VLAHOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Those are my questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Emmerson. Mr. Guy-Smith, any need for cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Harvey?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: No, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, any need to re-examine the witness? MR. DI FAZIO: No, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Vlahovic, the parties have no further questions for you. The Bench have no further questions for you either. Therefore, this concludes your testimony before this court. I'd like to thank you that you have come the far journey and that you've answered the questions of the parties. Madam Usher, could you please escort the witness out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Your Honours, the next witness in line is a witness who's been given, on the provisional list, a number 49. I'm so sorry, that is his pseudonym, 49.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: (redacted) None has been served.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: That is correct, if Your Honours please. My colleagues have been dealing with this issue, and (redacted) is, indeed, the next witness in line. I wonder, Your Honours, if -- and I understand that there's -- the witness has arrived here in The Hague. I wonder if Your Honours would be minded to defer the question of calling him until tomorrow. It's now ten to 7.00, and I need to confer with my colleagues concerning the provision of the statement to the Defence and ultimately to you, if that's going to be possible. I don't know what further developments have occurred during the day because I've been involved here in court. I'm unable to report to you at this stage, and I think that the Prosecution will be in a position to report to you on that issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: But not at this moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I did understand that Mr. Emmerson expressed concerns not only about not having had an opportunity to properly prepare for the witness to be called now, eight minutes to 7.00, but also about tomorrow. Is that correctly understood?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. The Prosecution has not fulfilled the promise that its made in respect to this witness, and we're in a position where, as I understand Mr. Di Fazio, there may even be a question about whether he's going to be called tomorrow. MR. DI FAZIO: That is so.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, if that's right, we're in a position where it's 7.00 at night, I have no idea what witness it is I am to cross-examine tomorrow. And can I indicate that the witnesses that follow in the Prosecution's list are Witness number 6 in the order of testimony - and there's no witness protection issues here - Dragoslav Stojanovic; and 7, Mijat Stojanovic. No proofing notes have been served in respect of either of those witnesses either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: Well, if Your Honours please, I don't believe there are any proofing notes in existence in relation to the Stojanovics.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is that because they -- you do not intend to proof them or that no notes were made of any proofing sessions until now? MR. DI FAZIO: Up until I came back into court, I was -- my understanding was that there were no proofing notes in existence in relation to those -- to the Stojanovics.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That still doesn't answer my question. My question was: Is it that they do not exist because you do not intend to proof, and of course prior to proofing, there will be no proofing notes; or that there have been proofing sessions but no proofing sessions were made or finalised? MR. DI FAZIO: I can certainly tell you that -- well, I believe up until I last came into court that there had been no proofing sessions and no proofing notes had been finalised. As to the intention to proof the witness, as I stand here, I simply don't know. I understood that that may not happen, but the matter was remaining with Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you. If Your Honours please, I can -- I'm happy to report to you that I can inform you that there have been no -- there has been no proofing of Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You're talking about Stojanovic. Let me go back to Witness 49. We received a message addressed to Mr. Re and, from what we understand, copied to Emmerson, Dixon, Troop, Rohan, Guy-Smith, Park, Aksenova, Trapani, Willemsen, van den Berge, Harvey, and the Haradinaj Trial Support, and it starts ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which announces that: "Attached are the proofing notes, the witness statement, and an English language of a draft consolidated statement." Do I then understand that your problem is that you didn't expect the draft but a signed final version of --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honour, I think, recalls the position that Mr. Re has been advocating that witnesses -- witnesses would be shown a statement in a language they understood, given an opportunity to correct it and to sign it. That is the proposal that the Prosecution committed to paper in a document that was filed this morning. It was also a proposal that was specifically made in respect of this witness. And, indeed, when those documents were supplied to us, they were supplied to us on the understanding that by the end of the day, that day, we would have an Albanian signed witness statement. And on that understanding, the Defence raised no objections to the material at all being supplied to the Trial Chamber, and so that we could be working from a common pool of materials. Nothing further has happened since then, and I don't know when Mr. Di Fazio says there's an issue about whether this witness is going to be called at all tomorrow, that is an issue which is solely contingent upon the fact that this document has not yet been signed or whether there are other concerns.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Di Fazio, we now have -- we know that, of course, information that was sent yesterday, we know that there's a draft consolidated statement. What caused the failure to send a finalised and signed statement to the Defence? MR. DI FAZIO: I understand the final stage of getting the signature on the document has not been achieved.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I think it would not be proper for the Chamber to ask at this moment why it has not been achieved. There could be a hundred reasons, some of them perhaps very varying; others perhaps very innocent.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I simply inquire whether the Prosecution proposes to call this witness tomorrow or not?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: We intend to -- yes, we intend to call him and get him to this courtroom, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. I think what we need at this very moment is that the Prosecution -- MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: -- whether that would then lead to testimony is a matter that I can't assure you about and I can't assure the Defence. So I can tell you this: Yes, we've reached the stage of a draft statement. We have not reached the stage of affixing of a signature to that draft statement. Yes, it is the intention of the Prosecution to bring the witness to court, and beyond that I simply don't have any more information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It will be a situation I have not met before in this Tribunal, that the witness is called and then not examined. But, okay -- MR. DI FAZIO: It is unusual, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is a bit mysterious. I think it would be inappropriate at this moment to ask -- further inquire with Mr. Di Fazio what happens, because it's his witness. He'll prepare for the testimony --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: May I make one matter absolutely plain: We would not be prepared, with respect, unless directed to do so to countenance the calling of the following witnesses before the provision of any proofing notes, if there are to be any. If there is to be no proofing session, then without notice, we're not going to find ourselves in a position to conduct cross-examination of those witnesses tomorrow. But, of course, that wouldn't preclude them being called - at least the first of them - being called to give evidence in chief. May I also raise one other matter. Your Honours have received now two sets of written submissions, one from the Defence and one from the Prosecution, on the procedure to be followed. Perhaps now is not an ideal time to be examining the Prosecution's proposal, but nonetheless there are statements both of fact and of law in the Prosecution's written document which we saw this morning which require correction. If Your Honours are of the view, having seen the sets of pleadings that you've already received, that you have enough information and argument before you to reach a decision, then obviously it's unnecessary for us to address further written arguments to you; but if it would assist the Bench in any way to have a further round of written pleadings, there are matters which require correction in the Prosecution's submissions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Have you considered further oral pleadings?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm very happy to deal with it as a matter of oral argument.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Because we might have additional time tomorrow in the afternoon. It's not for certain that --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm very happy to deal with this in the course of oral argument.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We'll further -- let me see. It's unclear whether Witness 49 will be called and, if called, give testimony. It is unclear whether the draft consolidated statement given to the Defence is a document which assists in any way in the preparation of cross-examination, because it's uncertain whether it is the document. Of course, I take it that you've read it. I must say, I have not read it yet. I can imagine -- but there's also the issue of risk of waste of time, that of course if only two or three words would be changed once we have a signed document, then of course the -- for preparation, it would -- MR. DI FAZIO: It I may assist, I don't think that's going to be a problem. That's not really the problem. It's not a question of changes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And if the witness is not prepared to put their name to the document and accept it as theirs, then its usefulness in cross-examination is obviously very substantially diminished.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, is there -- another matter is, is there an audio-recording of the proofing session of this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, there is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It does exist. MR. DI FAZIO: I believe it does, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: MR. DI FAZIO: Your Honours ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll finish just in one or two seconds. But I'd like to go into private session for a minute.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.
